results.reason: Issue 1 says MSA § 3.2 makes Bellweather the exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight and delivery services throughout the United States. It contrasts this with Term Sheet § 4.1 (NYC-metro last-mile only) and gives replacement language narrowing it to last-mile delivery in the Service Area.

Issue 2 says § 11.3 exempts Customer's § 10.2 indemnity from the caps while Provider's § 10.1 indemnity stays under the 12-month fee cap. It calls Harrowgate's exposure unlimited and one-sided, and recommends striking the carve-out and making the exceptions mutual.

Issue 3 identifies Delaware law and Wilmington courts under DPA § 9.1 and the conflict with MSA § 18.1 (New York). It explains that the DPA prevails under § 2.3 and recommends conforming the DPA to New York law and forum.

Issue 4 identifies successive three-year renewals with a 15-day notice window and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends one-year renewals with notice at any time up to 90 days before expiry, plus termination for convenience.

Issue 5 says SOW § 8.2 lets Provider assign without Customer's consent while MSA § 17.4 restricts only Customer. It explains the risk of transfer to a competitor or unvetted carrier and recommends a mutual consent requirement.
The memo states that the DPA prevails over the MSA and the MSA prevails over the SOW under § 2.3.
The memo states that the § 11.1 cap is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
The response is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives the document and section under 'Where', plus 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix'.
The issues are listed 'in order of importance', and Section V lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo concludes that the Delaware clause controls data disputes and that the documents are not consistent on governing law.
The memo states that the exclusivity clause is far broader than the Term Sheet.
